boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Pomona College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops in Claremont with directly published evening hours.

cards.title: Denny’s, 820 S Indian Hill Blvd
cards.subtitle: Claremont — open 24 hours
cards.notes: Use this round-the-clock diner for a late meal; check the location page again if a holiday visit is planned.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour sit-down option in Claremont.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its 820 S Indian Hill Blvd restaurant as open 24 hours.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists restaurant hours as open 24 hours.

cards.title: Chipotle Mexican Grill, 885 S Indian Hill Blvd
cards.subtitle: Claremont — daily until 10 PM
cards.notes: Order pickup or dine in before the posted 10 PM close; this location is near Interstate 10 and Indian Hill Boulevard.
cards.short_summary: A daily 10 PM pickup-and-dine-in option.
cards.evidence_claim: Chipotle lists this Claremont restaurant's hours as 10:45 AM–10 PM daily.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily restaurant hours through 10 PM and in-store pickup.

cards.title: Corky’s Kitchen & Bakery
cards.subtitle: 2213 E Base Line Rd, Suite 200 — daily until 10 PM
cards.notes: Plan a seated meal or bakery stop before the daily 10 PM close at this Base Line Road location.
cards.short_summary: A restaurant-and-bakery option open nightly until 10 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: Corky’s lists its Claremont location at 2213 E Base Line Rd and daily hours of 6:30 AM–10 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant page lists daily service until 10 PM.

cards.title: Elvira’s Finest Foods of Mexico
cards.subtitle: 415 W Foothill Blvd — Fri–Sat until 10 PM
cards.notes: Aim for Friday or Saturday evening for the latest posted close; Sunday through Thursday service ends at 9 PM.
cards.short_summary: Mexican restaurant with later Friday and Saturday service.
cards.evidence_claim: Elvira’s lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11 AM–10 PM at 415 W Foothill Boulevard.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours until 10 PM; other listed days close at 9 PM.

cards.title: Pizza N’ Such
cards.subtitle: 202 Yale Ave — Wed–Sat until 9 PM
cards.notes: Use pickup or dine in during the Wednesday–Saturday 9 PM window; Sunday and Monday close earlier at 8:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: Family-owned pizzeria with 9 PM midweek-to-weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza N’ Such lists Wednesday–Saturday hours of 11 AM–9 PM at 202 Yale Ave.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Wednesday–Saturday service until 9 PM and carry-out availability.

cards.title: Claremont Village Eatery
cards.subtitle: 232 W Bonita Ave — Saturdays until 9 PM
cards.notes: Make this a Saturday stop for the latest posted close; weekday service ends at 6 PM and Sunday service at 4 PM.
cards.short_summary: A Bonita Avenue eatery with a Saturday 9 PM close.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village Eatery lists Saturday hours of 6 AM–9 PM at 232 W Bonita Ave.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Saturday hours until 9 PM; it is closed Tuesdays.

cards.title: Eddie’s Italian Eatery
cards.subtitle: 1065 W Foothill Blvd — Fri–Sat until 9 PM
cards.notes: Plan for Friday or Saturday to use the latest posted dinner hours; Tuesday through Thursday and Sunday close at 8:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: Italian-American restaurant serving until 9 PM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Eddie’s lists Friday and Saturday hours of 11 AM–9 PM at 1065 W Foothill Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Official contact page lists Friday–Saturday service until 9 PM.

cards.title: Tutti Mangia Italian Chophouse
cards.subtitle: 102 Harvard Ave — Fri–Sat until 10 PM
cards.notes: Reserve or walk in for a Friday or Saturday dinner before the 10 PM close; posted hours are shorter on other days.
cards.short_summary: A Harvard Avenue dinner option with 10 PM Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Tutti Mangia lists Friday hours of 5–10 PM and Saturday hours of 4–10 PM at 102 Harvard Ave.
cards.access_notes: Official booking page lists Friday and Saturday service through 10 PM.

cards.title: Menkoi Ya Ramen
cards.subtitle: 333 W Bonita Ave — listed until 9:30 PM
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s live hours before leaving, then head to Bonita Avenue for a late ramen dinner.
cards.short_summary: A Bonita Avenue ramen restaurant listing a 9:30 PM close.
cards.evidence_claim: Menkoi Ya Ramen lists its address as 333 W Bonita Ave and posted hours until 9:30 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant page displays hours through 9:30 PM; confirm live hours before travel.

cards.title: House of Pong
cards.subtitle: 238 N Yale Ave — Fri until midnight; Sat until 11 PM
cards.notes: For the latest posted service, go Friday before midnight; Saturday closes at 11 PM and other listed nights earlier.
cards.short_summary: An Asian-fusion restaurant with a posted Friday midnight close.
cards.evidence_claim: House of Pong lists Friday hours of 11:30 AM–12 AM and Saturday hours of 11:30 AM–11 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant site lists Friday service until 12 AM and Saturday service until 11 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Pomona spaces for studying, making, gathering, art, and campus expression, with access cues grounded in College sources.

cards.title: Honnold-Mudd Library study rooms
cards.subtitle: Library study space
cards.notes: Use the study rooms for a focused work session, then keep conversation considerate of others sharing the library.
cards.short_summary: A documented study-room stop for solo work or meeting up with classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: A Pomona student tour guide says students study in Honnold-Mudd Library’s study rooms.
cards.source_title: Connect with a Tour Guide | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Library access and room-use rules may vary; check the library before planning a group session.

cards.title: Smith Campus Center Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center outdoor gathering space
cards.notes: Meet at an umbrella table or use the courtyard as a waypoint between classes; it remains a public passage space.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus-center courtyard with seating and direct connections to student services.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes the courtyard as a public space with umbrella tables and chairs, with access to campus-center services.
cards.source_title: Smith Campus Center Spaces | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: The courtyard is public, but reserved events may be in progress; leave paths and service access open.

cards.title: Coop Fountain
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center food-service venue
cards.notes: Use the Fountain as a campus-center meetup point or food stop, and check current dining details before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A long-running food-service location inside the Smith Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies the Coop Fountain as one of the food services on the Smith Campus Center’s main level.
cards.access_notes: Food and drink purchases are separate from simply passing through the Campus Center.

cards.entity_name: Rick and Susan Sontag Center for Collaborative Creativity (the Hive)
cards.title: The Hive
cards.subtitle: Maker and collaborative-creativity center
cards.notes: Drop in to explore a making activity or settle into a study session; ask staff about equipment and program access.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on creative space that also draws students looking for a welcoming place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the Hive combines a hands-on maker space with design courses and that some students come there to study.
cards.source_title: An Update on the Hive and Its Next Chapter | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Confirm current workshop, equipment, and building-access arrangements with the Hive.

cards.title: Marston Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Central campus lawn
cards.notes: Bring a book or meet a friend on the lawn between classes, while yielding to any scheduled campus programming.
cards.short_summary: Pomona’s central quadrangle, used as both a green space and an event setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies Marston Quadrangle as the center of campus, and its admissions materials place student activities there.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor common area; event setups may affect available lawn space.

cards.title: Walker Wall
cards.subtitle: Walker Beach free-speech wall
cards.notes: Read the current painted messages and, if you plan to contribute, follow the College’s wall guidance and community norms.
cards.short_summary: A campus forum where students use paint to share opinions and advertise events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says Walker Wall has served as a public forum for student expression and event advertising since the early 1970s.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Pomona College | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Painting is governed by College policies; review current guidance before adding anything.

cards.title: Victor Montgomery Music Library
cards.subtitle: Thatcher Music Building, Room 209
cards.notes: Use the study area, listening station, or seminar room for music-focused work, and check the posted library schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A music library with study seating, computers, listening resources, and space for small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the Montgomery Music Library has a study area, computer and listening stations, and a seminar room for study groups.
cards.source_title: Victor Montgomery Music Library | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: The College notes that hours are subject to change; verify access before heading over.

cards.title: Edmunds Ballroom
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center event space
cards.notes: Look for lectures, performances, or campus gatherings scheduled here, and use the room only when an event is open to you.
cards.short_summary: The Campus Center’s largest configurable venue for dining, audiences, and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes Edmunds Ballroom as the largest space in Smith Campus Center, with dining, audience, and performance setups.
cards.source_title: Smith Campus Center Spaces | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled events and reservations; do not enter during private programming.

cards.title: Mudd Lounge
cards.subtitle: Residential common-area lounge
cards.notes: Coordinate a recognized student gathering through the appropriate reservation process, and respect the residence-hall setting.
cards.short_summary: A residential common area available for organized academic, social, and co-curricular events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona’s housing policies list Mudd Lounge among residential spaces reservable for organized student events.
cards.source_title: HRL Policies and Procedures | Pomona College Catalog
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required for organized use; residential common-area events are substance-free.

cards.entity_name: James Turrell Skyspace, Dividing the Light
cards.title: James Turrell Skyspace
cards.subtitle: Draper Courtyard, Lincoln and Edmunds Buildings
cards.notes: Visit at a calm time to sit beneath the canopy and observe the sky; sunrise and sunset programs offer a longer experience.
cards.short_summary: A public art installation designed around changing light, sky, and quiet observation.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the public may visit Dividing the Light anytime and describes daily sunrise and sunset lighting programs.
cards.access_notes: The Skyspace is public and not reservable; no food or drink is permitted, and visitors should respect quiet enjoyment.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission activities at Pomona and nearby Claremont Colleges venues.

cards.entity_name: Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College
cards.title: Browse the Benton galleries
cards.subtitle: 120 W. Bonita Ave., Claremont
cards.notes: Meet at the galleries and take a slow lap through the changing exhibitions; no ticket or purchase is needed for museum admission.
cards.short_summary: A free, public art stop at Pomona’s museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Benton Museum of Art states that it is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Open during posted museum hours; check the visit page before going.

cards.entity_name: Benton Museum of Art Gallery Talks
cards.title: Join a Benton gallery talk
cards.subtitle: Benton Museum of Art, Pomona College
cards.notes: Check the museum’s weekly lineup, then join the short gallery talk and Q&A with artists, curators, students or staff.
cards.short_summary: An informal, focused art conversation in the galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Benton gallery talks are described as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current weekly schedule with the museum before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Pomona College Department of Music Concerts
cards.title: Catch a Pomona music concert
cards.subtitle: Pomona College performance venues
cards.notes: Use the Music at Pomona calendar to choose a department concert and arrive early enough to settle in before the performance.
cards.short_summary: Free public performances by Pomona’s music department.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona College states that all Music Department concerts are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Programs and venues vary; use the department calendar for the current listing.

cards.title: Hear the Friday Noon Concert
cards.subtitle: Balch Auditorium, Scripps College
cards.notes: Bring a friend to Balch Auditorium for the noon series, featuring faculty, visiting professionals and friends of the colleges.
cards.short_summary: A weekly midday classical-music option.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friday Noon Concert Series lists admission as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Friday Noon Concert Series | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Doors open at noon; confirm the active term’s schedule before attending.

cards.title: Attend a Concert Choir performance
cards.subtitle: Garrison Theater, Scripps College
cards.notes: Pick a listed Concert Choir date and listen with the community in Garrison Theater; check the program page for any updates.
cards.short_summary: A free public choral performance at Scripps.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joint Music Program says Claremont Concert Choir concerts are free of charge and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Choral Concerts - The Joint Music Program
cards.access_notes: The published 2026–27 schedule is subject to change; confirm date and time before going.

cards.title: Listen to the Treble Singers
cards.subtitle: Garrison Theater, Scripps College
cards.notes: Plan around a scheduled Treble Singers concert and arrive with time to find seating in the Garrison Theater.
cards.short_summary: A separate choral program with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joint Music Program says Claremont Treble Singers concerts are free of charge and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Choral Concerts - The Joint Music Program
cards.access_notes: The published 2026–27 schedule is subject to change; confirm date and time before going.

cards.title: See a Williamson Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: 251 E. Eleventh St., Scripps College
cards.notes: Visit during an exhibition window and spend time with the gallery’s current show; donations are welcome but not required.
cards.short_summary: Free public gallery admission on the Scripps campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ruth Chandler Williamson Gallery states that it is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open during exhibitions Wednesday–Sunday, 12–5 p.m.; verify exhibition dates first.

cards.title: Go to a Goudy Lecture
cards.subtitle: Honnold Library, Claremont Colleges
cards.notes: Watch Scripps’ lecture listings for the next Goudy talk, then pair the talk with a walk through the neighboring colleges.
cards.short_summary: Public talks centered on books, type and book arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps College states that Frederic W. Goudy Lectures are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Structures of Practice: Building Meaning Through Material and Form
cards.access_notes: Confirm the next lecture’s date, room and any attendance instructions on Scripps’ events pages.

cards.title: Reserve a free Scripps Presents program
cards.subtitle: Scripps College venues, Claremont
cards.notes: Choose a program explicitly marked free, reserve a seat if requested, and arrive before the ticket-holder seating cutoff.
cards.short_summary: Public cultural programs, with reservations often required.
cards.evidence_claim: Scripps Presents states that most of its programs are free and open to the public, with reservations required.
cards.access_notes: Only select listings explicitly identified as free; reserve seats through the current event listing when required.

cards.entity_name: City of Claremont Monday Night Concert Series
cards.title: Settle in for a Monday night concert
cards.subtitle: Memorial Park, Claremont
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or chair for the City’s summer concert series and enjoy the scheduled live performance in Memorial Park.
cards.short_summary: A City-run outdoor summer concert series.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Claremont describes its Monday Night Concert Series as a free eight-week series.
cards.source_title: 2026 Monday Night Concert Series Press Release | City of Claremont
cards.access_notes: This is a seasonal series; check the City’s current announcement for the lineup and weather updates.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, documented study environments in Pomona College’s shared Claremont Colleges Library and Mason Hall.

cards.title: Collaborative Commons
cards.subtitle: Honnold 2 North, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Set up with a partner at the media:scape tables, pivoting-table chairs, or modular seating; use the nearby Power Bar to charge devices.
cards.short_summary: A flexible open area built around collaborative seating and charging.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collaborative Commons is an open study area with modular seating, pivoting-table chairs, media:scape tables, and a Power Bar.
cards.access_notes: Located in Honnold 2 North; consult library building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Glass Bridge & Treadmill Desks
cards.subtitle: Between Honnold and Mudd, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring a lightweight task and work at a treadmill desk while looking out through the glass bridge’s treetop campus views.
cards.short_summary: A movement-friendly desk setting in the library’s connecting bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: Treadmill desks are located in the glass bridge between Honnold and Mudd and offer treetop campus views.
cards.access_notes: Between the Honnold and Mudd sides of the library; consult library building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Digital Scholarship Collaboratory
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 South, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Use this open area when dual monitors, visualization hardware, or specialized software would help move a digital project forward.
cards.short_summary: An open study area equipped for digitally intensive work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Scholarship Collaboratory is an open study area with dual monitors, a data visualization panel, and software suites.
cards.access_notes: Located in Mudd 2 South; consult library building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Study Cubes
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 North & South, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Choose a semi-private cube for a solo task or a small working conversation; the library says no reservation is required.
cards.short_summary: Semi-private cubes that support individual or small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Cubes in Mudd 2 North and South are semi-private spaces for individual or group study and do not require reservations.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required, according to the library; consult building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Third-Floor Open Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Honnold & Mudd 3, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Spread out reading, notes, and a laptop on the modular desks and tables in this open third-floor study setting.
cards.short_summary: Open third-floor seating with modular desks and tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Open study areas on Honnold and Mudd 3 feature ample open seating with modular desks and tables.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floors of Honnold and Mudd; consult library building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Honnold North & South, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Use the modular tables in the designated quiet area when you need minimal noise distraction for concentrated reading or writing.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study setting on Honnold’s fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnold fourth-floor quiet study areas provide ample open seating with modular tables and minimal noise distraction.
cards.access_notes: Located in Honnold North and South on the fourth floor; consult library building policies for current access details.

cards.title: Honnold 4 Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Honnold 4, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a project meeting that benefits from privacy, modular seating, and a whiteboard; room technology varies by room.
cards.short_summary: Reservable private rooms for group work and whiteboard planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnold 4 study rooms offer privacy, modular seating, and whiteboards; the library lists them as reservable study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Reservable rooms are available to current students, faculty, and staff; capacity and technology vary.

cards.title: Honnold 3 South Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Honnold 3 South, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Book a room for a focused group session, then use its modular seating and whiteboard to map out tasks or work through problems.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor reservable rooms configured for private study.
cards.evidence_claim: Study rooms in Honnold 3 South offer privacy, modular seating, and whiteboards and are reservable.
cards.access_notes: Reservable rooms are available to current students, faculty, and staff; capacity and technology vary.

cards.title: History Department Library
cards.subtitle: Room 121, Mason Hall, Pomona College
cards.notes: Read or write among the history collection; required History course texts are held in reserve, and student proctors can assist during listed hours.
cards.short_summary: A departmental reading and writing room with History course reserves.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona’s History Department Library in Mason Hall room 121 welcomes Claremont Colleges students and is described as a peaceful place to read, study, and write.
cards.access_notes: The page lists Monday–Thursday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; hours are subject to change. Claremont Colleges students are welcome.

cards.title: Mudd 1 Open Study Area
cards.subtitle: Mudd 1, Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Pair a research session with the nearby government documents, maps, microfilm, and print collections; the Main Services desk is nearby.
cards.short_summary: An open study area beside maps, government documents, and library collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Mudd 1 contains an open study space alongside government documents, maps, microfilm, and print book collections.
cards.access_notes: Located on Mudd 1; consult library building policies for current access details.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Claremont Village destinations on Yale Avenue, West First Street, and Harvard Avenue, immediately west of Pomona College.

cards.title: Folk Music Center & Museum
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 220 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Walk Yale Avenue to browse the named Folk Music Center & Museum, then check its official page for current lesson, repair, and appraisal services.
cards.short_summary: A Yale Avenue music destination with documented classes, repairs, and appraisals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Folk Music Center & Museum is located at 220 Yale Avenue and lists classes and lessons, appraisals, and repairs.
cards.access_notes: Check the official site for current hours and service availability.

cards.title: Some Crust Bakery & Cafe
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 119 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Use the Yale Avenue walk to stop at Some Crust Bakery & Cafe; the Village directory identifies the cafe by name and street address.
cards.short_summary: A named bakery and cafe directly on the Yale Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official shop-and-dine directory lists Some Crust Bakery & Cafe at 119 Yale Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; confirm current service details with the business.

cards.title: Hens' Kitchen Shoppe
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 141 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Pause along Yale Avenue to browse Hens' Kitchen Shoppe, a specifically listed kitchen-goods destination rather than an unnamed storefront.
cards.short_summary: A named kitchen shop on the Yale Avenue commercial corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists Hens' Kitchen Shoppe at 141 Yale Avenue under gifts and specialty shopping.
cards.access_notes: Retail items require purchase; verify current hours before making a special trip.

cards.title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 200 W. First Street, at the Claremont Depot
cards.notes: Walk West First Street to the museum entrance on the Depot's north side; Pomona students can enter without admission under the museum's student policy.
cards.short_summary: A First Street art museum in the historic Claremont Depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art is at 200 W. First Street in the Claremont Depot; students receive free general admission.
cards.source_title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Students are free; bring student identification and check the museum's current public hours.

cards.title: Claremont Depot
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 200 W. First Street
cards.notes: Use the historic Depot as a West First Street landmark: its north side faces First Street and houses the Claremont Lewis Museum of Art entrance.
cards.short_summary: A named historic depot anchoring the First Street edge of the Village.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art states that it is in the Claremont Depot at 200 W. First Street, with its entrance facing First Street.
cards.source_title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing does not require admission; museum access follows its published hours.

cards.title: Claremont Packing House
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 532 W. First Street
cards.notes: Continue west on First Street to see the 1922 Packing House and choose among its documented shops, restaurants, arts, and classes.
cards.short_summary: A preserved former citrus packing house repurposed for Village retail and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Packing House at 532 W. First Street is a historic Village landmark with shops, restaurants, arts, and classes.
cards.access_notes: Individual tenants and activities may have separate hours and charges.

cards.title: Forum Bookshop
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 586 W. First Street
cards.notes: Follow West First Street to Forum Bookshop to browse books, cards, bookmarks, and journals; purchases support the Prison Library Project.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit-linked bookshop whose sales support a books-to-prisoners program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Forum identifies its bookshop at 586 W. First Street and says purchases support the Prison Library Project.
cards.access_notes: Browsing is available during the bookshop's posted hours; merchandise requires purchase.

cards.title: JAX Bicycle Center
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 217 W. First Street
cards.notes: On the West First Street corridor, use JAX Bicycle Center as a named stop for bicycle-related retail or service needs before heading farther into the Village.
cards.short_summary: A specifically listed bicycle shop on West First Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists JAX Bicycle Center at 217 W. First Street.
cards.access_notes: Retail goods and shop services require purchase; confirm current service availability directly.

cards.title: Boon Companion Toys
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor • 145 Harvard Avenue
cards.notes: Turn onto Harvard Avenue for Boon Companion Toys, a named specialty retail stop listed at 145 Harvard Avenue in the Village directory.
cards.short_summary: A named toy store on the Harvard Avenue portion of Claremont Village.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists Boon Companion Toys at 145 Harvard Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail items require purchase; verify current opening details with the shop.

cards.title: Claremont Farmers & Artisans Market
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor • Claremont Village
cards.notes: Plan a Sunday Harvard Avenue walk around the Farmers & Artisans Market, where the Forum documents fresh produce, local farms, and handcrafted goods.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Sunday market on Harvard Avenue in Claremont Village.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Forum states that its Farmers & Artisans Market operates Sundays from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Harvard Avenue in Claremont Village.
cards.access_notes: The market is documented for Sundays, 8 a.m.–1 p.m.; vendors' goods are individually priced.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Pomona College rituals and recurring campus practices, from the number 47 to the commencement walk through the gates.

cards.title: The Number 47
cards.subtitle: Pomona College campus lore
cards.notes: Spot the number in campus life, then join the April 7 celebration of the student-and-alumni tradition.
cards.short_summary: An unofficial Pomona mascot born from a 1964 campus experiment.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says two students began tracking occurrences of 47 in 1964; it became an unofficial mascot and is celebrated on 4/7 Day.
cards.access_notes: Observe and participate only through announced campus activities.

cards.title: Birthday Fountaining
cards.subtitle: Pomona College fountains
cards.notes: If friends propose a birthday fountain celebration, make sure everyone wants to participate and plan for dry clothes.
cards.short_summary: Friends mark academic-year birthdays with a surprise fountain dunk.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona documents the practice of throwing a student into a campus fountain on their birthday during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Participate only with clear consent and follow campus safety guidance around fountains.

cards.title: Harry Potter Holiday Dinner
cards.subtitle: Frary Dining Hall, Pomona College
cards.notes: Check dining announcements in December for this Frary transformation, then attend through the dining hall’s normal access.
cards.short_summary: Frary becomes a Hogwarts-inspired dining hall for one December evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says Frary Dining Hall staff transform the space each December with house flags, butter beer and wizard-themed fare.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in December; confirm event details and dining access with Pomona Dining Services.

cards.title: Mufti Notes
cards.subtitle: Pomona College campus
cards.notes: Notice the cryptic campus-commentary notes as a piece of Pomona lore; do not remove, alter or imitate posted materials.
cards.short_summary: A secret society’s cryptic, figure-eight-glued messages offer campus commentary.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes Mufti as a secret society founded in 1958 that posts cryptic social-commentary notes in a figure-eight glue pattern.
cards.access_notes: View posted materials respectfully and comply with campus posting policies.

cards.title: Omelets at Frank
cards.subtitle: Frank Dining Hall, Pomona College
cards.notes: Visit Frank brunch and select omelet ingredients at the made-to-order bar when it is offered.
cards.short_summary: The custom omelet bar is a longstanding centerpiece of Frank brunch.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies made-to-order omelets, with diner-selected vegetables, cheeses and meats, as a key Frank Dining Hall brunch tradition.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current brunch service and dining access with Pomona Dining Services.

cards.title: Orientation Adventure
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation, Pomona College
cards.notes: Incoming students can review Orientation Adventure options and follow the College’s registration and trip guidance.
cards.short_summary: New students take three-day, student-led trips around Los Angeles.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says Orientation Adventure began in 1995 and sends new students on three-day wilderness, cultural and entertainment trips led by older students.
cards.access_notes: For incoming students during orientation; use official new-student communications for current options and requirements.

cards.title: Painting Walker Wall
cards.subtitle: Walker Wall, Pomona College
cards.notes: During orientation, work with your sponsor group on its assigned section and respect the wall’s role as a public forum.
cards.short_summary: Sponsor groups paint sections of Pomona’s recognized free-speech wall.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says Walker Wall has served as a student forum since the early 1970s, was recognized as a free-speech wall in 1975, and is painted by sponsor groups each fall.
cards.access_notes: Painting is part of New Student Orientation; follow sponsor-group and campus posting guidance.

cards.title: Ski-Beach Day
cards.subtitle: Pomona Events Committee annual spring event
cards.notes: Watch for the Pomona Events Committee announcement, then use the event’s arranged transport and activity instructions.
cards.short_summary: A spring day that pairs mountain snow with an Orange County beach visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says its annual Ski-Beach Day takes students by bus to Mountain High Resort in the morning and an Orange County beach afterward.
cards.access_notes: Annual spring event; confirm current eligibility, transportation and activity requirements with the Pomona Events Committee.

cards.title: Sponsor Groups
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation, Pomona College
cards.notes: Meet your assigned sponsor group early, use it for orientation questions and join its Walker Wall painting activity.
cards.short_summary: Small residence-hall cohorts connect new students with returning student sponsors.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says incoming students are assigned to sponsor groups of 10–20 hallmates led by older students who live among them and provide guidance.
cards.access_notes: Assigned before new students arrive; use official orientation communications for current details.

cards.title: Through the Gates
cards.subtitle: College Gates, Pomona College
cards.notes: Enter through the gates during New Student Orientation, then return for the outward walk during Commencement weekend.
cards.short_summary: Students ceremonially enter at orientation and leave through the same gates before commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says new students enter through the College Gates at orientation and, four years later, march through them in the other direction before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Orientation and pre-Commencement tradition; participate through the College’s scheduled ceremonies.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pomona College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented through Pomona’s campus landmarks, arts, and Claremont community spaces.

cards.title: Start at the College Gates
cards.subtitle: A first look at Pomona’s ceremonial entrance
cards.notes: Begin with a photo at the gates, then trace your route into campus. New students formally enter here during the documented Through the Gates orientation event.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial starting point for new Sagehens.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies Through the Gates at the College Gates as a traditional event where new students officially enter campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow current campus visitor guidance.

cards.title: Get your bearings on Marston Quad
cards.subtitle: The center of the Pomona campus
cards.notes: Use the quad as your campus reset point: notice the surrounding buildings, pick a direction for your next stop, and save the view for a return visit.
cards.short_summary: Pomona’s central quadrangle anchors the walking route.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona College’s catalog identifies Marston Quadrangle as the center of campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; access may be affected by college events.

cards.title: Read the current Walker Wall
cards.subtitle: Pomona’s recognized public-forum wall
cards.notes: Pause to see the wall’s current messages, then continue without adding anything yourself. Its changing painted surface makes it a useful snapshot of campus expression.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding campus wall used for public expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona’s timeline says generations of students have used Walker Wall as a public forum for painted messages.
cards.access_notes: Located by Walker Beach on the campus visitors’ map; view respectfully.

cards.title: Find Pegasus on Stover Walk
cards.subtitle: Stover Walk, north edge of Marston Quadrangle
cards.notes: Walk the east-west route along Marston Quad and look for the bronze Pegasus relief near College Avenue. It is a concrete waypoint before heading toward arts venues.
cards.short_summary: A named sculpture and historic campus walkway.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona documents Pegasus on Stover Walk near College Avenue and describes Stover Walk as a primary east-west campus axis.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route and artwork shown on the campus map; keep to pedestrian paths.

cards.entity_name: Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College
cards.title: Step into the Benton Museum
cards.subtitle: Rotating exhibitions at the campus–Village edge
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current visit information, then spend time with one exhibition rather than rushing through. The building’s courtyard is part of the campus-facing setting.
cards.short_summary: A free public art stop with rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona states that all Benton Museum exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and accessibility details before visiting.

cards.title: See Frary’s two murals
cards.subtitle: Prometheus and Genesis inside Frary
cards.notes: If you have appropriate dining-hall access, look up at the two documented murals while passing through. Treat the hall as an active dining space and follow posted rules.
cards.short_summary: A dining-hall stop with two significant murals.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona’s catalog identifies José Clemente Orozco’s Prometheus and Rico Lebrun’s Genesis as murals in Frary Dining Hall.
cards.access_notes: Dining-hall access and meal requirements may apply; verify current campus dining access.

cards.title: Check what’s on at Big Bridges
cards.subtitle: Concerts, lectures, and dance performances
cards.notes: Photograph the exterior, then check the current events calendar for an appropriate program. Attend only events whose posted entry requirements and timing work for you.
cards.short_summary: A landmark auditorium for major campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes Bridges Auditorium as a venue for convocations, concerts, lectures, and dance performances.
cards.access_notes: Event access, tickets, and hours vary; consult the current event listing.

cards.title: Learn where the campus farm is
cards.subtitle: A two-acre on-campus growing space
cards.notes: Use the campus map to locate the farm, then look for approved ways to engage with its programming. Do not enter growing areas or handle animals unless invited.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus farm with orchard and chickens.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes its on-campus farm as a two-acre space with chickens, a fruit orchard, and a student-built biodome.
cards.access_notes: The farm is map-listed; participation and entry depend on current college programming.

cards.entity_name: The Claremont Colleges Ballroom Dance Company
cards.title: Look for a Ballroom Dance Company event
cards.subtitle: A recurring performance and formal-ball activity
cards.notes: Check campus listings for a public lesson, performance, or formal ball and follow the organizer’s attendance instructions. It is a structured way to try a social campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A documented Claremont Colleges dance activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says The Claremont Colleges Ballroom Dance Company often presents performances and formal balls.
cards.access_notes: Schedules, locations, and participation requirements vary by event.

cards.title: Finish with Sunday market browsing
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue in Claremont Village
cards.notes: On Sunday morning, walk the market route on Harvard Avenue and browse produce, plants, and artisan stalls. Bring a payment method only if you intend to buy something.
cards.short_summary: A Sunday Claremont Village market with farm and artisan vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: The market’s official site lists Sunday hours of 8 a.m.–1 p.m., rain or shine, on Harvard Avenue between First Street and Bonita Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Sundays, 8 a.m.–1 p.m., rain or shine; Harvard Avenue between First Street and Bonita Avenue.
